data.name: Meenakshi
data.gender_notes: Meenakshi is used as a female name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit mīna, 'fish', + akṣi, 'eye' — 'fish-eyed', an epithet of Parvati. Its root is Sanskrit mīna + akṣi. Meenakshi, a form of Parvati worshipped at Madurai. Meenakshi is a Sanskrit name meaning “Fish-eyed; the goddess Parvati”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Meenakshi expresses “Fish-eyed; the goddess Parvati”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit mīna, 'fish', + akṣi, 'eye' — 'fish-eyed', an epithet of Parvati.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Meenakshi total 40, reducing to 4. Number 4 is associated with discipline, order and steady effort.

vedic_reference.note: Meenakshi is a popular Hindu female name, derived from the goddess Meenakshi, who is often depicted with fish eyes. The name is believed to have originated from the Sanskrit word 'mīnā' meaning 'fish' and 'ākṣī' meaning 'eyes'. In Hindu mythology, Meenakshi is believed to be an incarnation of the goddess Parvati, and is worshipped as the goddess of love, marriage, and fertility.
